messages:
leah: FYI support reported a tenant isolation anomaly in the sidebar metrics widget. customer 'Greenfield' saw CPU and token usage spikes that belong to another org for ~30s. attaching quick screenshot. :sweat_smile:

leah: reproduction: load customer console, open sidebar -> Metrics (last 1h) -> chart shows two series: greenfield-app and partnercorp-app (partnercorp is a different tenant)

tomas: which env and build? any canary traffic running?

leah: hit on prod-us-east. recent deploy at 2026-03-15T19:02:00Z rolled out route-affinity-cache change (affinity ttl extended from 10s -> 60s). seeing it since ~19:05. stacktrace in browser console is empty (widget is client-side), but network call is to /api/console/sidebar/metrics?range=1h

leah: request headers:
```
GET /api/console/sidebar/metrics?range=1h HTTP/1.1
Host: console.prod.redwood
x-route-affinity: af_9c1c
x-org-id: org_gf12
```
response body contains series with workspace_id: ws_pc77 (partnercorp)

jing: quick thought: route-affinity is used for sticky routing to specific backend pools. we added an optimization where route-affinity -> cached backend metadata includes last-handled-workspace to avoid extra metadata lookups. if that cache entry is shared across tenants on the edge, we could leak the last_handled workspace into responses if we accidentally surface backend metadata into response cache keys.

tomas: do we have a middleware that equivocates backend metadata into response headers? i remember a recent PR that added X-Backend-Meta for telemetry.

jing: yes PR#4472 added X-Backend-Meta: last_workspace=ws_<id> for debugging. it was gated but accidentally enabled in prod for the affinity rollout. that header was unintentionally included in the server-side render pipeline and also got serialised into the client-side widget cache key.

leah: ugh. so the widget uses a cached payload keyed by "sidebar:metrics:affinity=af_9c1c:range=1h" and that cached payload now includes a series tagged with last_workspace=ws_pc77. when a subsequent request from org_gf12 hits the same affinity key, it returns the cached payload.

ops-bot: automated mitigation suggestions:
- roll back header emission in backend (hotfix)
- invalidate sidebar:metrics cache for affected affinity ids
- revert affinity ttl change to 10s

tomas: immediate move: invalidate caches for recent affinity ids and flip the header flag off. i'll open a hotfix PR to remove X-Backend-Meta emission and coordinate a quick deploy.

jing: also adding a server-side assert: responses that are cached must include explicit workspace_id in the key and be rejected if backend_meta.last_workspace != request.workspace. snippet:
```
if cache_entry.backend_meta and cache_entry.backend_meta.last_workspace != req.workspace_id:
    raise CacheConfusionError()
```

leah: +1 on the assert. long-term we should stop shipping backend meta into response payloads at all. it's too easy to accidentally leak.

support-bot: customer Greenfield notified via INC-2026-119. initial mitigation applied (cache invalidation). support reports chart repaired after ~45s.

tomas: follow-ups:
1) backfill telemetry: add metric `sidebar.cache.cross_workspace_returned{org_id}` to detect if cache returned payload where included workspace != requester
2) add test that simulates mixed-tenant requests hitting same affinity key and verify no cross-tenant series
3) evaluate whether affinity ttl increase from 10s->60s is worth the risk - maybe we constrain to internal-only pools

jing: on (1) i'll add telemetry tag `cache_workspace_assertion` with values pass/fail and a Grafana panel alert when fail > 0

leah: on (2) i'll add an integration test in console-e2e that spins up two tenants, forces same affinity id via stubbed routing, and validates isolation. will file PR after hotfix.
tomas: on (3) ops to review affinity policy. reverting TTL for now.

ops-bot: cache invalidation completed for affinity ids: af_9c1c, af_4d2b, af_ee11. job id: inv-17688.

leah: quick note - quota attribution check: if metrics or token counts were misattributed, billing could be affected. tomas can you run quick reconciliation for last 1h for affected orgs?

tomas: will run quota reconciliation job and post results in INC-2026-119.

jing: internal API debate: should route-affinity carry any mutable backend metadata? leaning toward no. we should store opaque affinity pointers and resolve metadata per-request in a safe context. i'll open an RFC.

leah: thanks everyone. I'll draft a short postmortem and link PRs here. closing thread and moving follow-ups to INC-2026-119 and console PRs. :writing_hand:
